name: manual_961e8c
claim: When building schema validation or a packaging format that mirrors an external tool's spec (e.g. Anthropic's packaged-skill frontmatter rules), fetch that tool's actual source (quick_validate.py-style scripts, not just prose docs) and reimplement from the real rules -- don't infer limits/allowed-fields from documentation prose or memory, which can be stale or incomplete.

decisions.notes: Building orama-system's package_skill.py (.skill packaging for skillify), fetched anthropics/claude-plugins-official's actual quick_validate.py and package_skill.py source rather than guessing at the 1024-char description limit, the exact ALLOWED_PROPERTIES set, or the zip-exclude patterns. Confirmed the docs-prose numbers (from an earlier ad-hoc Cowork session's dogfood-upgrade-log.md) were accurate, but having the real source made the reimplementation provably correct rather than plausible.
